On Friday I am having dinner with my parents; we already booked a table.
planes.explanation: Para un plan ya organizado con otra persona se usa el presente continuo.

wrongAnswers.answer: On Friday I will have dinner with my parents; we already booked a table.
wrongAnswers.why: 'Will' no es lo más natural para un plan ya arreglado con mesa reservada; corresponde el presente continuo.

planes.instruction: Traducí la oración al inglés usando la forma de futuro adecuada.
planes.spanish: Quizás visite a mis primos en España el año que viene.
answers: Maybe I'll visit my cousins in Spain next year.
Maybe I will visit my cousins in Spain next year.
planes.explanation: Con 'maybe' se usa 'will' para expresar una predicción incierta.

wrongAnswers.answer: Maybe I'm going to visit my cousins in Spain next year.
wrongAnswers.why: Con 'maybe' se prefiere 'will' para expresar una predicción incierta, no 'going to' que implica mayor certeza.

wrongAnswers.answer: Maybe I visit my cousins in Spain next year.
wrongAnswers.why: Falta el auxiliar 'will' para expresar la predicción futura.

planes.instruction: Traducí la oración al inglés usando la forma de futuro adecuada.
planes.spanish: Creo que va a llover mañana.
answers: I think it will rain tomorrow.
I think it'll rain tomorrow.
planes.explanation: Con 'I think' para expresar una opinión sobre el futuro, sin evidencia visible, se usa 'will'.

wrongAnswers.answer: I think it rains tomorrow.
wrongAnswers.why: El presente simple no se usa para predicciones futuras.

wrongAnswers.answer: I think it's going to rain tomorrow.
wrongAnswers.why: Con 'I think' se expresa una opinión sin evidencia visible; en ese caso se prefiere 'will' y no 'going to'.

planes.instruction: Traducí la oración al inglés usando la forma de futuro adecuada.
planes.spanish: Camila se muda a Mendoza el mes que viene; ya compró los pasajes.
answers: Camila is moving to Mendoza next month; she already bought the tickets.
Camila's moving to Mendoza next month; she already bought the tickets.
planes.explanation: Cuando el plan ya tiene evidencia concreta (pasajes comprados) se prefiere el presente continuo.

wrongAnswers.answer: Camila will move to Mendoza next month; she already bought the tickets.
wrongAnswers.why: 'Will' no es lo más natural para un plan ya organizado con pasajes comprados; corresponde el presente continuo.

planes.instruction: Traducí la oración al inglés usando la forma de futuro adecuada.
planes.spanish: Probablemente me quede en casa este fin de semana.
answers: I'll probably stay home this weekend.
I will probably stay home this weekend.
planes.explanation: 'Probably' se coloca entre 'will' y el verbo base, que nunca lleva 'to'.

wrongAnswers.answer: I will probably to stay home this weekend.
wrongAnswers.why: El verbo nunca lleva 'to' después de 'will'; además 'probably' va entre 'will' y el verbo.

wrongAnswers.answer: Probably I will stay home this weekend.
wrongAnswers.why: En inglés lo natural en este tipo de frase es colocar 'probably' entre 'will' y el verbo, no al principio de la oración.

planes.instruction: Leé el texto y respondé las preguntas eligiendo la opción correcta.
planes.text: Hi! I'm Sofía, and I want to tell you about my plans. Next month, I'm going to visit my sister in Bariloche because we already bought the bus tickets. I'm meeting her at the bus station on Friday afternoon. We're going to visit the lake and maybe go skiing if there's enough snow. I'll probably bring my camera because the mountains are beautiful in winter. One day, I'd like to learn to ski really well, but for now, I'll just try my best. My sister thinks it will be very cold, so I'm going to pack warm clothes. In two weeks, I'm also having a dentist appointment before the trip. I hope everything goes well!

questions.prompt: Why is Sofía going to visit her sister next month?
options: Because they already bought the bus tickets.
Because her sister invited her last week.
Because she has a dentist appointment there.
Because she wants to learn to ski.
questions.explanation: Se usa 'going to' porque ya hay una decisión tomada con una prueba concreta: los pasajes de micro ya comprados.

questions.prompt: What is already arranged for Friday afternoon?
options: Sofía is having a dentist appointment.
Sofía is meeting her sister at the bus station.
questions.explanation: El presente continuo se usa para planes ya organizados con fecha y hora fija, como 'I'm meeting her on Friday afternoon'.

questions.prompt: What does Sofía's sister think will happen with the weather?
options: She thinks it will be very cold.
She's going to check the weather before leaving.
She thinks it will probably be warm.
She knows it will snow a lot.
questions.explanation: 'Will' se usa para expresar una predicción basada en una opinión, como la de la hermana sobre el frío.

planes.instruction: Leé el texto y respondé las preguntas eligiendo la opción correcta.
planes.text: Diego is talking to his friend Pablo about his future plans. Next year, Diego is going to start English classes because he wants a better job. He already registered at a language school near his house. On Monday, he's having an interview for a new position at a travel agency in the city center. He thinks the interview will go well because he practiced a lot. 'I'll probably be nervous,' Diego said, 'but I'll do my best.' Soon, he's also going to visit his grandparents in Rosario, since he hasn't seen them in months. One day, Diego would like to open his own travel agency, but for now, he's focusing on his English and his new job. Pablo thinks Diego's plans will come true.

questions.prompt: Why is Diego going to start English classes next year?
options: Because the travel agency asked him to.
Because he wants a better job.
Because he will travel to Rosario.
questions.explanation: 'Going to' se usa para planes con una razón o decisión previa, como querer un trabajo mejor.

questions.prompt: What is already arranged for Monday?
options: Diego is having an interview at a travel agency.
Diego is opening his own agency.
questions.explanation: El presente continuo describe un plan ya organizado con día y hora fijos, como la entrevista del lunes.

questions.prompt: What does Diego say about how he will feel at the interview?
options: He says he will ask Pablo to come with him.
He says he'll probably be nervous but will do his best.
He says he won't be nervous at all.
He says he will cancel the interview.
questions.explanation: 'Will' junto con 'probably' se usa para suavizar una predicción sobre cómo se va a sentir, y también como promesa de esforzarse.
